correctness.rationale: The two-particle configurations are isolated; the first derivative consists of the zero configuration and the singleton orbit, with two further derivatives giving the zero configuration and then the empty set. Normalize an automorphism by its unique shift on the singleton orbit. A radius-R local rule fixing zero and all singletons fixes every pair of gap greater than 2R. On the remaining free shift orbits equivariance gives a gap permutation and an independent translation on each orbit. Conversely finite support bounds both the gaps affected and the coordinate displacements, so the resulting bijection and its inverse are continuous at the singleton and zero limits. Equivariance gives the stated restricted semidirect product and the unchanged global shift is central. The infinite simple finitary alternating subgroup dies in every finite quotient. A finitely generated subgroup acts on only finitely many gap labels after dividing out global shifts; its intersection with the resulting finite-rank free abelian subgroup has finite index. The language count, zero entropy and unique periodic point follow by counting supports. The finite verification script is diagnostic only and was not executed.

evidence: For b>=3 the indexed power-gap examples have at most two occupied sites. The decisive radius proof uses only that every occupied pair with gap >2R looks locally like at most one particle. Salo's Corollary 3 concerns a product with a full shift; the Salo–Törmä paper is about rank two.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The indexed proof transfers to any infinite set of permitted pair gaps if no third particle is permitted; both proof directions work with the unchanged outlying gaps and arbitrary finite permutations of the allowed gaps.
